Study: parents of toddlers were randomly assigned either to text-message vaccination reminders or to carry on as usual.
Groups: text-message vaccination reminders (n = 600) and usual practice (n = 600).
Outcome: on-time vaccination, in percent of children (higher is better).
Result: mean 72.0 (text-message vaccination reminders) against 72.2 (usual practice); difference -0.2 (95% interval -2.4 to 2.1).
The outcome was measured once, one week after the start.

Study: primary-school pupils were randomly assigned either to a free school breakfast or to carry on as usual.
Groups: a free school breakfast (n = 110) and usual practice (n = 110).
Outcome: attendance, in days per 60-day term (higher is better).
Result: mean 55.0 (a free school breakfast) against 53.2 (usual practice); difference 1.9 (95% interval 0.8 to 3.0).

Study: ninth-grade algebra students were randomly assigned either to weekly peer tutoring or to carry on as usual.
Groups: weekly peer tutoring (n = 35) and usual practice (n = 35).
Outcome: end-of-term exam score, in points out of 100 (higher is better).
Result: mean 64.9 (weekly peer tutoring) against 63.4 (usual practice); difference 1.5 (95% interval -5.5 to 8.5).
Everyone in the study came from a single school.
